intro: The captain died with the map in his head. Luckily for the crew, he was a paranoid man, and he had it tattooed, in pieces, on each of them. The bosun keeps the captain's chart table in the great cabin, and its side is a long row of pigeonholes, each cut to take one thing and one thing only. No man can slip his piece into a neighbour's hole; the pieces are not interchangeable, and the table will not forgive a wrong fit. The crew are learning the shape of their own pieces by trying them against the holes, one at a time, until each arm finds the place that holds it.
echo: Fletcher Christian took the Bounty. The crew here are considering something similar.

puzzles.title: The Brig
puzzles.flavor: Shredded, then sorted by a very tidy intern.
hints: The strips are alphabetised, not in order. The word lengths say where the breaks fall. Which strip could start the sentence?
Chain the strips into one string and split it by the word lengths; the sentence tells you what to submit.

puzzles.title: Walk The Plank
puzzles.flavor: Shaken, one word at a time.
hints: Each word is complete but shuffled. Start with the shortest ones: does a sentence appear?
Unscramble each word where it stands; the sentence tells you what to submit.

puzzles.title: Shiver Me Timbers

blocks.text: Hidden in the grid: 10 words to do with the ship.

hints: Once every theme word is found, is anything left unclaimed? Read it in order.
Find the theme words; the letters no word uses, read row by row, are the answer.
The hidden words are: BOSUN, HAMMOCK, HOOK, HULL, ISLAND, KEEL, LIME, PARROT, SAIL, SPYGLASS.

puzzles.title: Articles
puzzles.flavor: The spy always carried a novel. This page will have to do.

blocks.text: The captain died with the map in his head. Luckily for the crew, he was a paranoid man, and he had it tattooed, in pieces, on each of them.

hints: The first number in each pair never goes past the number of words on the page. What does the second count?
The first number finds a word on the page; the second finds a letter in it.

puzzles.title: Letter Of Marque
puzzles.flavor: A familiar grid, an unfamiliar alphabet.
hints: A familiar grid puzzle in unfamiliar clothes. Once it's done, are some squares more important than others?
Solve it like a sudoku, then read the numbered squares in order.

puzzles.title: Crow's Nest
puzzles.flavor: A formula no chemist would sign.
hints: Everything here has a number in a famous chemical line-up. What number does each one have?
Atomic numbers, then count through the alphabet (hydrogen = 1 = A).

meta.title: Meta: Dead Men's Chest
meta.flavor: Pigeonholes, each cut to fit one thing only.
hints: The grid's rows are all different lengths. So are your answers.
Put each answer in the row its length fits; read the shaded squares top to bottom.
